Prototype note
Option B reveals from the right so that Before stays on the left and After on the right, as in A and C. The approved home hero wipes from the left.

Before-and-after slider options

Three ways to show the Lilim House living room as handed over and as furnished. Each works with mouse, touch, and the arrow keys. Each respects reduced motion. Option A is recommended.

A. Classic drag handle

Recommended
Complexity
Low. One component with pointer and key handling.
Accessibility
Strongest. A slider you can reach by keyboard, moved with arrow keys, Home, and End. No motion.
On phones
Reads clearly. The 44 px handle is the touch target, and vertical swipes still scroll the page.
Why recommended
It behaves the same with mouse, touch, and keyboard, it costs the least, and a visitor knows how to use it. The scroll wipe (B) stays on the hero.
Deviation
The handle is a 2 px radius square, because the locked system allows no circles.
After
Before

B. Scroll-driven wipe in a pinned frame

Used for the hero pair on both project pages.
Complexity
Medium. It reuses the approved home hero wipe, driven by scroll position. A hold of 96 px on desktop and 80 px on phones follows the reveal.
Accessibility
There is no control to operate, so keyboard and screen reader users meet both frames as plain images. Under reduced motion, the two frames sit one above the other.
On phones
It reads well but takes about 520 px of scroll per pair. That suits one hero pair and tires over five.
Before
After

C. Hover or drag reveal

Complexity
Medium to high. It needs pointer-type detection and a one-time nudge.
Accessibility
It uses the same slider as A, so keys work. A moving mouse changes the picture without intent, which can annoy people who have tremors or who read with the pointer. The nudge is skipped under reduced motion.
On phones
It becomes a drag handle, the same as A. The hint is a single slide of the line, with no text, so it keeps the rule against hint text.
